title: Couples Therapy: When to Go, What to Expect, and Does It Work?
description: Is couples therapy right for you? What happens in sessions, different approaches, when to go (and when it's too late), and how to find a good couples therapist.

content.text: Couples therapy isn't just for relationships on the brink. It can help good relationships become great and struggling ones find their footing. Here's what to know.

items: Major life transitions (kids, job changes, empty nest)
Proactively wanting to strengthen the relationship

content.text: When Individual Therapy Might Be Better First

items: Active addiction that isn't being addressed
One partner refusing to participate genuinely
Severe untreated mental illness in one partner
Initial assessment: understanding the relationship history and current issues

content.text: Focuses on attachment and emotional bonds. Helps partners understand the emotions driving their conflicts and create new, positive interactions.
Research-based approach targeting the 'Four Horsemen' (criticism, contempt, defensiveness, stonewalling) and building friendship, conflict management, and shared meaning.
For 'mixed-agenda' couples where one wants to work on it and one wants to leave. Helps clarify whether to commit to couples therapy or separate.
Research shows 70% of couples who complete therapy show improvement, with effects lasting years for many. Emotionally Focused Therapy shows 70-75% recovery rates.
Success depends on: both partners' commitment, therapist skill, timing (earlier is better), and willingness to do work between sessions.

items: Look for specific couples therapy training (not just any therapist)
Ask about their approach and experience with your issues
Both partners should feel comfortable with the therapist

content.text: Couples therapy works—but timing matters. The average couple waits 6 years from when problems start to seek help. Don't wait until you're on the brink. If the same fights keep happening or you feel disconnected, therapy can help you find your way back to each other.
